Select the adverbials of time in the paragraph.

feedback.end: The adverbials of time “last Monday” and “next Monday” add cohesion to the paragraph by connecting the two events.

atoms.b: ((Last Monday,)) my mum went to the shops and bought a new top, but she realised that it had a large hole in it. ((Next Monday,)) she is going to take it back to the shop.

instruction.text: Select the adverbials of place in the paragraph.

feedback.end: The adverbials of place “at the beach” and “near the beach” add cohesion to the paragraph by linking the two sentences together.

atoms.b: My brother went on holiday this weekend. He spent lots of time ((at the beach)). ((Near the beach,)) there were lots of ice-cream shops and restaurants.

instruction.text: Select the adverbials of number in the paragraph.

feedback.end: The adverbials of number “firstly” and “secondly” add cohesion to the paragraph by creating a time line of events.

atoms.b: Robert is learning how to knit. ((Firstly,)) he buys all the tools that he needs, including needles and wool. ((Secondly,)) he looks online to find tutorial videos.

trainers.instruction: Choose the correct adverbials to fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: ((++Last_weekend, Next_weekend,)) I went to Paris. Paris is a beautiful city and I saw lots of amazing tourist attractions. ((++Near_the_river, Next_year,)) there was a market, where I bought some beautiful artwork. ((++Lastly, Firstly,)) I went to a restaurant to get some food before flying home.

trainers.instruction: Use all the adverbials to correctly fill in the gaps. Remember to add a comma where needed.

atoms.b: ((Last_year,)) we got a dog and named her Daisy. ((At_first,)) she was very timid and unsure of her surroundings. She even hid from us under the sofa! ((After_a_while,)) she became comfortable with us.
